## Summary
Claude usage patterns, customisation architecture, development workflows, and behavioural guidelines for LLM-driven coding, plus the emerging practice of using Claude as a personalised AI thinking partner and building taxonomy-driven, self-improving organisational knowledge agents. This cycle adds two agent-infrastructure frameworks: MASTRA (TypeScript-native agent/workflow library) and Temporal (durable-execution orchestration for crash-resilient agent loops).

## Key Insights
- Claude has four usage modes: end user, Claude Code builder, API builder, automation. MCP scopes: user, local, project.
- Customisation hierarchy: System Prompt -> Project Instructions -> User Preferences -> Custom Styles -> MCP Tools/Skills.
- Skills are Capability Uplift (new tools, needs code execution) or Encoded Preference (behaviour only, SKILL.md).
- Karpathy's CLAUDE.md guidelines: think first, minimalism, surgical changes, goal-driven verifiable execution.
- Structured docs (ADR/PRD/BDD) are the control surface for autonomous agents; ADRs are CI-enforced.
- Being AI-native = workflow readiness and context accessibility, not doing everything with AI.
- CLAUDE.md as a personal self-portrait; naming/identifying an AI shifts instruction-giving into dialogue; memory tracking builds a longitudinal self-knowledge layer ("Pippi" model).
- Company/knowledge-agent pattern: small JSON taxonomy anchors agent semantics; two-agent split (news/ingestion vs. deep research); active curation loop prevents knowledge rot; typed knowledge-graph edges over flat rows; self-improving gap-filling loop; budget/model tiering (Haiku/Sonnet/Opus) with daily spend caps; source validation protocol; freshness "temperature" tagging.
- MASTRA: Apache-2.0 TypeScript agent/workflow framework, unified model router, library-not-SaaS.
- Temporal: durable-execution platform, Event History replay, workflow (deterministic) vs. activity (non-deterministic) split maps cleanly onto agent loops.

## Summary
Structural/behavioural design principles for LLM-guided software, the Backend-for-Frontend (BFF) API pattern, CQRS/knowledge-system architectures separating write and read paths, and durable-execution orchestration (Temporal) for agent loops. A company-brain thread frames shared ontology as an architectural pattern bridging Conway's Law silos.

## Key Insights
- Think first, simplicity first, surgical changes, goal-driven verifiable execution (Karpathy CLAUDE.md guidelines).
- ADRs are CI-enforced architectural boundaries, not just docs; PRD+BDD chains product intent to executable specs.
- BFF pattern: client-specific API aggregation (web vs mobile) behind a shared API Gateway that owns cross-cutting concerns (auth, rate limiting, logging, compression).
- CQRS in practice (Sanity): PostgreSQL as immutable append-only write ledger; Elasticsearch inverted index for all reads; Pub/Sub propagates writes to caches/search.
- Referential integrity via typed pointers instead of SQL joins; asset pipelines split binary (object storage + CDN transforms) from structured text/metadata.
- Knowledge-system architecture: JSON taxonomy for semantic anchoring, two-agent specialisation (ingestion vs. research), ontology for relationships (graph, not flat rows), mandatory curation loop, budget/model tiering, self-improving gap-filling loop.
- Temporal: Service + Client SDK + Workers; determinism is the core constraint (workflows replay from Event History, non-deterministic work pushed into retryable Activities); incremental adoption extracts only long-running processes; Temporal (code-first) vs. Conductor (declarative DSL) is a real orchestration-substrate tradeoff.

## Summary
Strategic and philosophical perspectives on AI adoption alongside concrete PM framing for positioning and measuring AI-driven products: AI-native readiness, ecosystem-centric platform KPIs, the "stay human vs. maximise speed" design north star, and a role-specific AI skill map for product managers.

## Key Insights
- Being AI-native is workflow readiness, not "AI for AI's sake"; ask "can this be optimised with AI?" rather than "should we use AI?".
- Category commoditisation forces repositioning (Sanity: Headless CMS -> "Content OS for the AI Era") to escape price pressure and target higher-value budgets.
- Platform PM framing balances developer-facing metrics (velocity, API performance) against non-technical user metrics (time-to-publish); pair adoption metrics with quality/trust metrics (error rates), not adoption alone.
- The AI product design goal ("stay human" vs. "maximise speed") determines the entire interaction model; giving an AI identity shifts users from commanding to conversing.
- Taxonomy-driven knowledge management and the curation loop are product features/reliability concerns, not ops afterthoughts.
- AI as organisational intelligence layer bridges Conway's Law silos; SaaS shifts from ready-built software to composable primitives.
- PM AI skill gap: most companies plan AI integration but few PMs feel confident beyond basic chat use -- directing AI at product problems (not becoming a data scientist) is the differentiating, premium-priced skill.

bodies.wiki/cloud-infra:
## Summary
Seeded by a deep-dive into Sanity's Content Lake infrastructure: managed databases, search indexes, object storage, and CDN edge caching on Google Cloud powering a CQRS content platform.

## Key Insights
- Write path: PostgreSQL on GCE as an immutable, append-only ACID ledger.
- Read path: Elasticsearch serves all queries via an inverted index; PostgreSQL is never woken for reads.
- A GKE compute layer replicates Postgres writes to Elasticsearch and broadcasts change events via Cloud Pub/Sub to invalidate edge caches globally.
- Binary assets go to GCS with a lightweight reference pointer in the core datastore; GKE workers extract metadata (dimensions, palette, LQIP).
- On-the-fly asset transforms are handled by a serverless image-processing microservice at the Cloud CDN edge on a cache miss, then cached.

## Sources
- [Sanity's Content Lake](https://app.notion.com/p/37e59bb53cde81a89759ea3c7e0bf73e)

## Summary
Deliberate skill and knowledge development, particularly reflective and meta-cognitive practices that enable deep learning rather than rapid throughput -- the build-to-learn principle, structured AI-guided learning flows, and custom teaching tools.

## Key Insights
- Build from the inside out: replicate others' workflows only to understand the space, then build your own from your own priorities and cognitive style.
- Meta-learning via Claude: asking the AI to explain itself is high-leverage; it can narrate its own reasoning and design.
- Writing/blogging as a forcing function to slow down and move from execution mode into synthesis mode; token limits force reconnection with the real world.
- CLAUDE.md as a reflective exercise -- writing a personal profile is itself identity-building, not just configuration.
- Build-to-learn: AI guides via a /learn skill but the human types and builds, avoiding passive vibe-coding; scaffold with AI, then verify comprehension independently; build custom teaching tools tailored to personal goals.

bodies.notes/mastra-typescript-native-ai-agent-:
**Date**: August 21, 2026

MASTRA is an open-source (Apache 2.0) TypeScript framework for building AI agents, created by the Gatsby team; graduated Y Combinator (W25, $13M), hit v1.0 in January 2026.

- Primitives: `createAgent` (autonomous, LLM decides call sequence), `createTool`, `createWorkflow` (deterministic pipelines).
- Model Router: single interface across dozens of LLM providers -- provider swaps become config changes.
- Memory: observational memory persists conversation context and learns about users automatically.
- Production features: input/output guardrails, human-in-the-loop tool approval, native MCP support, OpenTelemetry tracing, Mastra Studio for local dev.
- Deployment: any Node.js environment, first-class Vercel/Netlify/Cloudflare, embedded (in-process) or standalone server modes.
- TypeScript vs Python is an ecosystem-fit choice, not an architectural one; MASTRA itself is backend-capable.
- Framework-as-library: you import and own the infrastructure; free framework, pay only LLM providers.
- Adoption: Replit, SoftBank, PayPal, PLAID, Marsh McLennan.
bodies.notes/temporal-durable-execution-for-ai-:
# Temporal: Core Knowledge Extracted

Temporal is a durable-execution platform guaranteeing workflow completion even after crashes, network outages, or infrastructure failures, via an immutable Event History that is replayed on recovery.

## Architecture
- **Temporal Service**: Frontend (gRPC/auth), History (Event History = source of truth), Matching (Task Queues), Persistence (Cassandra/MySQL/Postgres/SQLite); self-hosted or Temporal Cloud.
- **Client SDK**: embedded in your app; starts/signals/queries workflows, never executes workflow code.
- **Workers**: execute workflow + activity code in your own infrastructure; stateless and scalable.

## Execution model
- Workflows are deterministic orchestration code (no direct clock/random/I-O); replay from Event History reconstructs state.
- Activities handle non-deterministic I/O (LLM calls, DB queries, APIs); retryable, results cached in Event History.

## AI agent orchestration
Workflow = deterministic loop/decision structure; Activities = LLM calls + tool invocations. Gives durability across crashes and avoids re-paying for already-completed LLM calls on replay; supports child workflows/signals for multi-agent orchestration and 24/7 ambient agents.

## Temporal vs. Conductor
Temporal: code-first, event sourcing, tight orchestration/business-logic coupling, natural for AI agents. Conductor: JSON DSL, explicit DB state, orchestration separated from services, better for polyglot microservice coordination.

## Deployment & cost
Temporal Cloud (~$200-5k/month, 99.9-99.99% SLA, multi-region) vs. self-hosted (~$2.5-4.5k/month infra, full control, higher ops burden). Key gotchas: determinism, no direct I/O in workflows, replay complexity, versioning required for safe deploys.
bodies.notes/7-ai-skills-pms-should-master-befo:
Medium article by Mohit Aggarwal (Sep 27, 2025, ~4 min read). Framing stat: ~73% of companies plan to integrate AI into product development by 2027, but only ~23% of PMs feel confident using AI beyond basic ChatGPT queries -- that gap is the opportunity.

1. **AI-driven user research** -- analyse thousands of interviews/tickets in minutes (Dovetail AI, Claude for synthesis).
2. **Automated competitive intelligence** -- agents scrape competitor data 24/7 and deliver daily briefings.
3. **Predictive product analytics** -- shift from descriptive to predictive metrics (adoption, churn, pricing sensitivity).
4. **Intelligent roadmap prioritisation** -- feed sentiment, effort, and impact data into a model for data-backed prioritisation.
5. **Automated prototype/wireframe generation** -- Uizard, Figma AI, Adobe Firefly; prompt engineering as its own skill.
6. **AI-enhanced A/B testing** -- multivariate tests with smaller samples (Netflix: 250+ concurrent AI-driven tests).
7. **Natural-language PRDs** -- turn meeting transcripts into structured PRDs with acceptance criteria via Otter.ai + Claude/GPT-4.

Reality check: these are becoming table-stakes; London tech firms reportedly pay a 20-30% premium for AI-fluent PMs. Goal isn't becoming a data scientist -- it's fluency in directing AI at product problems.

bodies.notes/personal-ai-thinking-partner-claud:
A talk by the creator of the "Pippi" personal AI system. Core thesis: optimise for staying human and keeping judgment in the lead -- not for speed or automation.

## CLAUDE.md as self-portrait
Use CLAUDE.md to describe *you* -- thinking style, needs, communication style, correction patterns -- evolving as a mirror of your cognitive style as corrections feed back in.

## Key skills
- **GrowthMD**: reads mistake log + CLAUDE.md + past sessions -> "tough love" reflection on gaps between goals and behaviour.
- **LoveMD**: celebrates visible growth (Fridays / before vacations).
- **Morning skill**: reviews goals, todos, Slack, calendar -> flags misalignment between stated priorities and actual time use.

## Named AI identity (Pippi)
Naming the AI shifts instruction-giving into conversation -- you get challenged back.

## Mindprint starter guide
13 reflective questions -> AI generates a personalised CLAUDE.md, via a "fresh start" or "cognitive layer" track; free, public, no GitHub required.

## Meta-insight
Repeated personalised AI use teaches you about your own thinking, decisions, and communication -- value flows both directions.
bodies.notes/knowledge-graph-architecture-for-c:
Continuation of a talk on building a company AI brain (Data Mobility). Focuses on structuring knowledge as a graph rather than a flat database, and how the system self-improves.

## Graph over rows
Knowledge stored as nodes with typed relationships (funded by, piloted by, related to); queries return semantic clusters, not lists.

## Visualisation
Knowledge graph shown in an iframe; clusters form organically by domain activity; clicking a node shows its sub-graph and a generated summary.

## Self-improving loop
Build a summary -> flag what's unknown -> fire new research searches to fill gaps -> repeat, evolving without explicit user direction.

## Five takeaways
1. Taxonomy first (small JSON file of domain vocabulary, injected everywhere).
2. Simple continuous agents running overnight.
3. Structured storage/retrieval suited to volume (e.g. Voyage + Supabase).
4. MCP/CLI access so non-technical users and agents can query directly.
5. Self-evolving design: agents surface gaps and fill them.
bodies.notes/company-ai-knowledge-agent-multi-a:
A mobility data company describes their two-agent AI knowledge system for staying on top of a specialised domain.

## Agents
- **Pulse** (news scout): ingests 44 newsletters nightly at 4am, surfaces 3 items worth deeper research.
- **Research agent** (Scout/Scalchi): picks up Pulse suggestions, user requests, or Slack drops; validates sources and populates the knowledge base.

## Source validation protocol
Checks URL reachability, hallucination risk, paywall access, and whether the article actually supports the claimed insight.

## Budget and model mix
$20/day autonomous budget, $100+/day user-directed; Haiku for classification, Sonnet for most tasks, Opus for deep research.

## Temperature tagging
Each insight tagged with a review cadence (daily for breaking stories, every 6 months for stable regulation) to prevent staleness without over-fetching.

## Storage & Slack integration
RAG via Voyage embeddings + Supabase; agents follow Slack channels and ambiently ingest dropped reports.
bodies.notes/building-a-personal-ai-thinking-pa:
Insight from a talk by someone who built their own personal AI system (named Pippi) from scratch.

## Learning approach
Used Claude to learn about Claude; started by replicating others' workflows, then realised they were spending more time adapting to others' ways of working than building their own -- decided to build from the inside out.

## What they optimised for
Not speed, not productivity, not automation -- "how do I stay human in my interactions with AI?": maintaining judgment, staying in the lead, ensuring AI pushes you rather than replacing you.

## Mechanisms
- Writing/blogging as a forcing function to slow down and reflect.
- Token limits as an unexpected forcing function to reconnect with the real world.
- CLAUDE.md as a personal profile describing who you are, not project/automation descriptions.

## Key takeaway
The "stay human" / "build from the inside out" frame produces fundamentally different AI systems than optimising for speed.
bodies.notes/building-a-company-second-brain-ta:
Key insight from a talk on structuring company knowledge for AI agents.

## The problem
Knowledge lives in agent threads, Atlassian products, or Drive folders -- never becomes shared insight, isn't maintained, and is hard to find after the first week.

## Core concepts
- **Taxonomy as a JSON file**: define the domain (topics, subtopics, keywords) and inject it into agent prompts to anchor meaning (e.g. "mobility" = urban transport, not HR).
- **Ontology matters**: build a knowledge graph, not just a document store -- taxonomy gives structure, ontology gives relationships.
- **Two-agent architecture**: Pulse (daily news) feeds the brain; Scalchi does deep research and maintenance.
- **Knowledge curation loop**: agents must actively curate, validate, and maintain relevance, not just ingest.

## Speaker context
Data Mobility (New York) -- advising cities on shared mobility, needed domain-specific knowledge reliably available to agents.
bodies.notes/sanity-s-content-lake-cqrs-archite:
Interview prep briefing for a PM interviewing for Sanity's Content Lake / Content Platform domain.

## 1. Market positioning
Sanity is shifting from commoditising "Headless CMS" to a "Content Operating System for the AI Era": Sanity Canvas (visual ideation tied to structured Field Labels), native Functions (event-driven automation inside Sanity), and MCP-based AI-native structuring (agents read/write directly against the schema).

## 2. Technical architecture (CQRS)
Schema-less JSON core with validation declared upstream in code; referential integrity via typed pointer references (no SQL joins).
- **Write path**: Delta Patches into PostgreSQL on GCE as an immutable, ACID, append-only ledger.
- **Sync**: GKE layer replicates Postgres -> Elasticsearch and broadcasts via Cloud Pub/Sub to invalidate edge caches.
- **Read path**: Elasticsearch inverted index serves all GROQ queries; PostgreSQL is never woken for reads; bitwise intersections replace table scans.

## 3. Asset pipeline
Text -> Portable Text via the JSON/Elasticsearch pipeline; binaries -> Google Cloud Storage with a lightweight reference pointer; GKE workers extract metadata (dimensions, palette, LQIP); on-the-fly CDN-edge transforms cached after first request.

## 4. Human-in-the-loop AI workflow
Example: an event-driven Function detects a content change, fires an AI translation Agent Action into a staging area (Content Releases); a human gatekeeper reviews/polishes before publishing.

## 5. Interview framing
- Prioritisation: balance developer velocity/API performance against editorial time-to-publish, avoiding tech debt from bridges like Field Labels.
- Postgres-as-ledger + Elasticsearch-as-index resolves the transactional-vs.-scalable-reads tension that a single document store (e.g. MongoDB) can't.
- North-star KPI for the AI Content Agent/MCP tools: ratio of programmatic vs. manual mutations, alongside mutation error rate.
bodies.notes/bff-implementation-web-vs-mobile-r:
Concrete code patterns for implementing the BFF (Backend for Frontend) architecture, showing how a shared endpoint serves different clients with different response shapes.

- **Web BFF** (Node/Express): aggregates products + reviews + wishlist + AI recommendations + SEO metadata + full pagination.
- **Mobile BFF** (Node/Express): serves the same endpoint from Redis cache with a minimal shape (`id, name, price`) and lightweight pagination.
- **API Gateway middleware** (NGINX): validates auth, applies per-client rate limits, gzip compresses, logs with a request ID, and routes by user-agent to the mobile or web BFF.
bodies.notes/bff-architecture-pattern-client-sp:
The Backend for Frontend (BFF) pattern introduces a dedicated API aggregation layer tailored per client type (web, mobile), sitting behind a shared API Gateway and in front of core backend microservices.

Flow: Clients -> BFF (client-specific) -> API Gateway (shared middleware: auth, rate limiting, tracing) -> Core Backend Services -> DB + Cache.

- Web BFF: full data, pagination metadata, SEO fields, recommendations, wishlist.
- Mobile BFF: compact JSON, Redis-cached, offline support, minimal fields.

Separation of concerns: the Gateway owns auth/rate-limiting/logging/caching-headers; the BFF owns data shaping, service aggregation, and data-layer caching, and is the only layer aware of client type.
bodies.notes/being-ai-native-means-workflow-rea:
Being AI Native doesn't mean making everything with AI -- it means shaping your workflow so you're ready to make the switch: being conscious of AI tools, improving workflows to provide the right context, and connecting parts so AI can eventually have programmatic access.

Practical prep: being aware of recording meetings, writing decision documents, and writing things down generally.

The right question isn't "AI first" but "can this be optimised with AI?" -- evaluate AI fairly as part of the technology stack; if results aren't good enough, don't force it, but don't dismiss it either.
bodies.notes/structured-documentation-for-ai-as:
Source: *BDD, ADR, PRD, WTF: Capturing Decisions for Humans and AI Alike* -- Michal Cichra, Safe Intelligence.

## Core problem
Both humans and LLMs suffer from limited context; engineers (and autonomous AI agents especially) forget *why* code paths were built without explicit structured documentation.

## Formats
- **ADR**: documents why an architectural choice was made and how to enforce it; CI rejects commits that violate it and links agents back to the relevant ADR.
- **PRD**: tracks why a feature exists and the user's journey, as a reference frame once original intent is forgotten.
- **BDD (Cucumber)**: executable, human-readable specs bridging PRDs and working code, making AI-generated tests reviewable.

## Constraining AI in UI design
Strict design systems/pattern libraries with rigid rules force agents to compose predictable layouts instead of visual chaos.

## Enforcement loop
Git hooks + CI check linting, types, structural rules, and doc compliance; violations are rejected and linked back to the ADR/PRD to fix.
bodies.notes/llm-agent-coding-behavioral-guidel:
Behavioral guidelines from Andrej Karpathy's CLAUDE.md to reduce common LLM coding mistakes.

1. **Think Before Coding**: state assumptions, surface tradeoffs, ask when confused rather than guessing.
2. **Simplicity First**: minimum code that solves the problem -- no speculative features, abstractions, or unrequested error handling.
3. **Surgical Changes**: touch only what you must; don't refactor unrelated code; match existing style; only clean up dead code your own changes created.
4. **Goal-Driven Execution**: transform tasks into verifiable goals (e.g. "write a failing test, then make it pass"); state a brief plan with verify steps for multi-step tasks.

bodies.notes/claude-code-mcp-three-scope-levels:
### claude.ai MCP
Added in the UI; applies globally across all chats and projects, separate from Claude Code.

### Claude Code MCP -- Three Scopes
- **user**: available globally across all projects (e.g. GitHub, search tools).
- **local** (default): per-user, per-project (e.g. a project's database or Sentry instance).
- **project**: written to `.mcp.json` in the project root, committable to git for team sharing.

### Config storage
`local`/`user` scopes both live in `~/.claude.json` (local keyed by project path, user global); `project` scope lives in `.mcp.json` at the project root.
bodies.notes/four-ways-to-use-claude-from-chat-:
Claude can be used in four distinct modes:
- **End user** -- chat interface for goals like planning or learning.
- **Builder with Claude Code** -- Claude as a development partner.
- **API builder** -- custom applications via the Claude API.
- **Automation** -- speeding up and automating recurring workflows (Claude Code automation, Chrome plugin).
bodies.notes/claude-customization-layers-from-s:
claude.ai customization options: Project instructions, user preferences, writing styles, MCP tools, and skills. Claude Code uses CLAUDE.md, MCP tools, and skills for project-level customization.

**Customization hierarchy:** System Prompt (API-level) -> Project Instructions -> User Preferences -> Custom Styles -> MCP Tools.

- **System Prompt**: API-only; recommended structure is ROLE -> CONTEXT -> BEHAVIOR -> CONSTRAINTS -> OUTPUT.
- **Project Instructions**: persistent context in claude.ai projects; also useful for iterating on system prompts before persisting them.
- **User Preferences & Writing Styles**: claude.ai only -- account-level defaults vs. per-chat writing style.
bodies.notes/claude-skill-system-skill-md-forma:
Skill format is common to both claude.ai and Claude Code, using a `SKILL.md` file.

**Where skills live:** claude.ai (upload a zipped folder); Claude Code globally (`~/.claude/skills`); Claude Code per-project (`.claude/skills`).

**Types:**
- **Capability Uplift Skills**: grant new capabilities (e.g. web scraping, PDF creation); need `SKILL.md` + `scripts/` + `resources/`, dependencies, and code execution enabled.
- **Encoded Preference Skills**: define a behaviour pattern (e.g. commit message format); `SKILL.md` only, no dependencies, works anywhere.
bodies.notes/claude-prototyping-to-production-w:
## Prototyping vs Building
Use claude.ai for concept and prototype, Claude Code locally for writing code. Project Instructions in claude.ai serve as rough drafts for system prompts before production.

**Three layers:** RUNTIME (API system field, per-request), DEVELOPMENT (CLAUDE.md, lives in the repo), PROTOTYPING (Project instructions in claude.ai, iteration-friendly).

## Recommended workflow
1. Prototype on a claude.ai Project (ideate, validate, design APIs, decide architecture).
2. Distill decisions after each session into CLAUDE.md.
3. Code with Claude Code, which reads CLAUDE.md for full decision context.
4. Sync updated CLAUDE.md + key artifacts back to the claude.ai Project.
5. Repeat.

Handoff prompt: *"Summarize all the decisions we've made in this session into a CLAUDE.md format I can paste into my project."*
bodies.questions/what-are-the-key-goals-and-wor:
Suggested answer -- synthesised from notes: Four Ways to Use Claude, Claude Customization Layers, Claude Prototyping-to-Production Workflow.

Claude supports four distinct usage modes: (1) end user -- chat interface for goals like planning or learning; (2) builder with Claude Code -- Claude as development partner; (3) API builder -- custom applications via the Claude API; (4) automation -- recurring workflows via Claude Code or extensions.

Effective use requires customisation at the right layer: System Prompt for API-level control; Project Instructions in claude.ai for persistent project context; User Preferences for account-wide defaults; MCP Tools and Skills for capability extension.

Recommended workflow: prototype in claude.ai using Project Instructions as a scratchpad, then transition to Claude Code for implementation using CLAUDE.md for project-level context. Handoff prompt: "Summarize all decisions we've made into a CLAUDE.md format I can paste into my project."
